Package io.mavlink4j.session

Interface Dispatcher

public interface Dispatcher
Fan-out of decoded frames to subscribers, filtered by MessageFilter.

The one rule that matters

With subscribe(io.mavlink4j.session.MessageFilter, java.util.function.Consumer<io.mavlink4j.codec.Frame>), handler runs synchronously on the RX thread that decoded the frame, and must not block. This dispatcher does not queue and does not retry — a handler that needs to buffer (a slow HTTP/SSE push, a message-bus producer) uses subscribeAsync(io.mavlink4j.session.MessageFilter, java.util.function.Consumer<io.mavlink4j.codec.Frame>) instead of blocking here. A handler that throws is logged and isolated: it never prevents another subscriber from receiving the same frame, and never kills the read loop.

    • subscribe

    • subscribeAsync

      AsyncSubscription subscribeAsync(MessageFilter filter, Consumer<Frame> handler)
      Registers handler for every frame filter matches, but runs it on a thread of its own: the RX thread only enqueues. The queue is bounded by dispatchQueueCapacity and drops the oldest frame when full — a stalled consumer needs the newest data once it catches up, and a slow consumer must never stall reception. A handler that throws is logged and skipped. Close the returned subscription to stop the thread.
